This seems a regression. This is runnable in both 1.4 and 2.0 and works correctly in 1.4 but not on v2
```py
from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import (
    Computed,
    Text,
    func,
    select,
    text as _sa_text,
    create_engine,
    Column,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import TSVECTOR
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes import Integer

Base = declarative_base()

class Section(Base):
    __tablename__ = "sections"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    text = Column(Text)
    search_vector = Column(
        TSVECTOR,
        Computed(func.to_tsvector(_sa_text("'english'"), func.trim(text))),
    )

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Section({self.id=}, {self.text=}, {self.search_vector=})"

engine = create_engine("postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)

def main(conn) -> None:
    with Session(conn) as session:
        session.add(Section(text="faith"))
        session.flush()
        tsquery = func.plainto_tsquery(_sa_text("'english'"), "faith")
        section_query = (
            select(Section)
            .filter(
                Section.search_vector.bool_op("@@")(tsquery),
            )
            .subquery()
        )
        headline_query = select(
            section_query.c.id,
            func.ts_headline(
                _sa_text("'english'"),
                section_query.c.text,
                tsquery,
                _sa_text("'StartSel=**, StopSel=**'"),
            ).label("text"),
            section_query.c.search_vector,
        )
        aliased_query = select(Section).from_statement(headline_query)
        result = session.scalars(aliased_query)

        print("----------")
        print(vv := list(result))
        assert vv[0].text == "**faith**"

with engine.connect() as conn:
    Base.metadata.create_all(conn)
    main(conn)
```

well we would assume it's not matching up the column "text" here so it's just not getting loaded.

i dont think we quite expected from_statement() to do the text matching thing in this specific case, this would usually be from an `aliased()` that include `adapt_on_names=True`.   or `from_statement(text().columns(...))`.   it seems like `from_statement(select(foo.label('a_column')))` might need more hints that we are matching on name.   or we figure out what was in 1.4; in 1.4 it likely figured out that the "text" expression derived from the Section.text column originally.

here, this works instead, which should be good enough for now (it makes an extra subquery but should not be that big of  a deal unless this query is at the core of your high speed trading system)

```py
        ent = aliased(Section, headline_query.subquery(), adapt_on_names=True)
        aliased_query = select(ent)

```

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`column_property` breaks ORM insert from select with returning model.

This issue was introduced in version 2.0.2`.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.3

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

pysqlite

### Database Vendor and Major Version

SQLite

### Python Version

3.11

### Operating system

OSX

### To Reproduce

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select, insert, literal
from sqlalchemy.orm import MappedAsDataclass, Mapped, mapped_column, DeclarativeBase, Session, column_property

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", echo=True)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class User(MappedAsDataclass, Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(init=False, primary_key=True)

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column()
    age: Mapped[int] = mapped_column()

    is_adult: Mapped[int] = column_property(age >= 18, default=None)


Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

with Session(bind=engine) as session:
    stmt = select(
        literal(1).label("id"),
        literal("John").label("name"),
        literal(30).label("age"),
    )

    insert_stmt = (
        insert(User)
        .from_select(["id", "name", "age"], stmt)
        .returning(User)
    )

    result = session.scalars(insert_stmt)
```
